newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, HK executives unworried by '97 handover.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, HK executives unworried by '97 handover.

text.p: Most Taiwan and Hong Kong businesses are not worried about bilateral economic ties after the British colony reverts to China in July 1997, a Taiwan survey showed on Wednesday.
The survey of 95 major Hong Kong and Taiwan firms was conducted by the Chinese National Federation of Industries, one of Nationalist-ruled Taiwan's two main business associations.

Some 98 percent of respondents said investment ties would improve or remain unchanged for Taiwan businesses after the handover, while all said such ties would improve or remain unchanged for Hong Kong businesses.
The survey did not identify the respondents.
As for trade links, 60 percent of respondents said ties would improve or remain unchanged for Taiwanese firms after mid-1997 while 92 percent said this would be the case for Hong Kong firms.
Taiwan has banned all direct contact with China since a civil war split them in 1949. All Taiwan trade and investment in China must be routed through a third region, usually Hong Kong.
Since a political thaw between Taiwan and China began in the late 1980s, some 25,000 Taiwan businesses have spent over US$20 billion in China.
Yet despite business optimism, Taiwan said in early November that Hong Kong -- under pressure from China -- has started to restrict visits to the colony by Taiwan officials.
To maintain its ban on direct contact with Beijing, Taiwan has said it would treat Hong Kong as a special territory after the transition rather than as a part of the Chinese mainland.
